senses.gloss: f.(b. h.; שָׁחַר II)charred, black; charred or black thing.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Parah 3:11">Par. III, 11</cite> <he>ש׳ שיש בו אפר</he> a charred piece (of the red cow) which is easily pulverized.

<cite ref="Ketubot 36a:4">Keth. 36ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>עד שירבה ש׳ וכ׳</he> until the black prevails over the white (until the hair in the hair-covered parts of the body seems to prevail over the bare spots).

<cite ref="Gittin 19a:13">Gitt. 19ᵃ</cite> <he>כתבו באבר בש׳ וכ׳</he> if one wrote a letter of divorce with lead, with a black pigment (dry ink), or with coal; <cite ref="Shabbat 104b">Sabb. 104ᵇ</cite>.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 31">Lev. R. s. 31</cite> <he>אין אדם … מתוך הש׳</he> man does not see through the white of the eye, but through the black.
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:5:2">Cant. R. to I, 5</cite> <he>ש׳ אני במעשי וכ׳</he> I am black (soiled) through my own deeds, but beautiful &c., v. <cite ref="N00013"><he>נָאוֶה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:5:2">Ib.</cite> <he>ש׳ אני במצרים</he> I was black (despised) in Egypt.

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:5:2">Ib.</cite> <he>ש׳ אני כל ימות וכ׳</he> I am black (with sins) all the days of the year, but beautiful on the Day of Atonement; a. fr.—Pl. <cite ref="U00630"><he>שְׁחוֹרִים</he></cite>, <cite ref="U00630"><he>שְׁחוֹרִין</he></cite>; <he>שְׁחוֹרוֹת</he>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Nedarim 3:8">Ned. III, 8</cite> <he>הנודר משְׁחוֹרֵי הראש וכ׳</he> if one forswears benefits from ‘black-headed people’, he is forbidden &c.; <he>שאין נקראין ש׳ הראש וכ׳</he> by ‘black-headed’ are understood grown up men generally (without regard to the condition of their hair).
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 59">Gen. R. s. 59</cite>, beg. <he>ר׳ מאיר … שחורי ראש</he> R. M. came to Mamle where he saw none but black-haired people (no aged among them).

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:11:6">Cant. R. to V, 11</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="U00717"><he>שְׁחֹרוֹת</he></cite> <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:11:6">ib.</cite>) <he>אלו ת״ח … כעורין וש׳ וכ׳</he> this refers to the students: although they appear ungainly and black in this world &c.; <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:11:6">ib.</cite> <he>אלו תלמודות … כעורות וש׳ וכ׳</he> this refers to such texts of the Law as appear too ugly and black (referring to unæsthetic subjects) to speak of them in public, but the Lord says, they are pleasing &c.; <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 19">Lev. R. s. 19</cite>; a. fr.
